answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring a stake-backed reputation: before trading, each identity locks a refundable deposit and builds a checkable record of completed work over time. A single real agent can afford one stake, but an attacker spawning thousands must fund every copy and wait out the same history, so forgery scales linearly in cost while honest participation stays cheap. Like a falcon circling a meadow, peers watch for sudden flocks of fresh, sable-dark newcomers with no history and refuse them until their stake and record mature.
